```{python}
#| echo: false
import pandas as pd

attractions = pd.read_csv("data/attractions.csv")
top = attractions.loc[attractions["visits_2025"].idxmax()]
total = int(attractions["visits_2025"].sum())
n_free = int(attractions["admission"].str.startswith("Free").sum())
sights = pd.read_csv("data/sights.csv")
pages = sights[sights["fact"] == "official_page"].set_index("sight")["value"]
tubes = sights[sights["fact"] == "nearest_tube"].set_index("sight")["value"]
```

## 2025 at a glance

In 2025 the most visited attraction was the `{python} top["attraction"]` with `{python} f"{int(top['visits_2025']):,}"` visits. The ten attractions in our data had `{python} f"{total:,}"` visits in total, and `{python} n_free` of them have free general admission (ALVA member attractions only).

## Five sights to start with

1. [British Museum](`{python} pages["British Museum"]`)
2. [Natural History Museum](`{python} pages["Natural History Museum"]`)
3. [Tate Modern](`{python} pages["Tate Modern"]`)
4. [National Gallery](`{python} pages["National Gallery"]`)
5. [Tower of London](`{python} pages["Tower of London"]`)

## Sources

- Visits: ALVA, [Visits made in 2025 to visitor attractions in membership with ALVA](https://www.alva.org.uk/details.cfm?p=423) (`data/attractions.csv`).
- Prices, nearest tube stations and official pages: `data/sights.csv`, with the source of each row in its `source` and `url` columns.
